output.summary: A large tree abundant in northern and central inland Portugal and long known in the Iberian Peninsula. Its chestnuts were a major Portuguese staple until the 17th century and are still commonly eaten roasted or boiled in autumn. Its high-quality wood has been used for construction, furniture and interior decoration.
output.edibilityNote: Chestnuts were historically a Portuguese staple and are now commonly eaten roasted or boiled in autumn.
